thread:
Mika: Heads-up — planning a staged rollout for audit schema v4 next week. Primary goals: add safety gates, make KMS usage explicit (but masked), and provide a customer sandbox/dry-run bundle. Need alignment on sample payload content and customer communications.

Anna: I can own the comms and sample pack. Quick clarifying Qs: which KMS events do we want to show in samples? key_encrypt/key_decrypt/key_rotate? And do we show key_id masked or omit entirely?

Samir: Yes — runtime will emit key_encrypt, key_decrypt, key_rotate. We'll include a masked key_id field in samples (e.g., "proj-***-abcd"). Schema v4 also adds top-level fields: "safety_gate" (enum) and "redaction_level" (none/partial/full). Default: partial for hosted, full for private.

Jeff: For customer-facing validation: supply an "audit-validator" tool they can run against the sandbox bundle. It should detect required fields and flag PII. Also confirm embeddings: we should never include raw embedding vectors in audit events — only hashed or aggregate metadata.

Lina: Customers repeatedly ask for a workspace where they can map events to SIEM. Proposal: package a sandbox bundle (sample events + SIEM mappings + ingestion configs) and a quickstart script.

security-bot: Deploy scheduled: audit-schema-v4 -> staging at 2026-03-22T03:00Z (job 46231).

Mika: Important policy note for doc: list fields we will never include in audit events: user_password, raw_input_for_embeddings, full_card_number, unmasked_ssn. Make that an explicit "never-logged" section in the customer docs.

Anna: Draft is up: https://docs.internal.redwood/audit/v4/draft — added a section "never-logged" and sample payloads with masked key_id. Can reviewers please comment by EOD Friday? We'll send canary invites next Tuesday.

Samir: Operational detail: during rollout the runtime will emit both v3 and v4 for ~2 weeks. We add header `X-Audit-Schema: v4` when v4 is used. Storage/retention tooling needs to be able to filter on that header. Also adding an internal flag `audit_dry_run=true` for canary customers so events flow but are not forwarded to default SIEM endpoints.

Jeff: Customer changelog language: emphasize that v4 is additive (no breaking renames), includes safety gates to reduce accidental leakage, and provides sample mapping files for Splunk/Datadog/Elastic. Call out the audit-validator tool.

Lina: I'll assemble the sandbox bundle. Quick snippet to include in the docs for customers to run locally:

```bash
# validate sample bundle
audit-validator --bundle ./redwood-audit-sandbox-v4.tar.gz --mode dry-run
```

Anna: Also adding a short example payload (in the sample pack) showing a KMS access event with masking: 

```json
{
  "event_type": "key_decrypt",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-22T03:05:12Z",
  "key_id": "proj-***-abcd",
  "actor": "service_account:embedder-1",
  "safety_gate": "model_input_redaction",
  "redaction_level": "partial"
}
```

Mika: Thanks. Final asks before we cut the canary invite: (1) docs add explicit mapping table for v3->v4 fields, (2) release notes include exact timeline and fallback plan, (3) support playbook updated with steps to opt a customer out of forwarding during dry-run.

Samir: I'll update runtime release notes and add the header handling in the S3 ingestion filter.

Jeff: I'll draft the release note blurb and the support playbook snippet.

Anna: Putting a checklist in the doc and pinging legal for wording on customer-facing risk language. Will push draft updates by tomorrow morning.

Mika: Great — thanks everyone. If there are any compliance red flags call out in-thread or ping me directly. :thumbsup:
